label: After Utrecht and Rastatt
why: The War of the Spanish Succession is settled by Utrecht, Rastatt and Baden, fixing a European balance of Bourbon Spain, Habsburg Austria, Britain, France and the Dutch, while the Great Northern War still runs, the Qing are at their Kangxi peak and the Mughals are in decline after Aurangzeb.

realms.name: Kingdom of Great Britain
realms.note: Formed by the Acts of Union 1707 from England and Scotland; North American and Caribbean colonies; Gibraltar and Minorca gained at Utrecht.

realms.name: Kingdom of Ireland
realms.ruler: George I (governed by a Lord Lieutenant and Lords Justices)
realms.note: Separate kingdom with its own parliament, under the British crown.

realms.name: Kingdom of France
realms.note: Keeps Alsace, Franche-Comté and Lille region; lost Newfoundland, Acadia and Hudson Bay at Utrecht; New France and Louisiana in America.

realms.name: Spain (Bourbon monarchy)
realms.note: Map id of Castile used for the Spanish monarchy; the Nueva Planta decrees (1707-1716) fold the Crown of Aragon into it. Lost its Italian lands and the Southern Netherlands at Utrecht and Rastatt; holds the Spanish Indies and the Philippines.

realms.name: Kingdom of Portugal
realms.note: Restored in 1640; Brazil (gold boom in Minas Gerais), Angola, Mozambique, Goa, Macau.

realms.name: Republic of the Seven United Netherlands
realms.ruler: States General; Grand Pensionary Anthonie Heinsius (Second Stadtholderless Period)
realms.note: With the VOC (Batavia, Ceylon coast, Malacca, Cape) and WIC (Suriname, Curaçao, Elmina).

realms.name: Habsburg Monarchy (Austria)
realms.ruler: Charles VI (Holy Roman Emperor; King of Bohemia and Hungary)
realms.note: Gains Milan, Naples, Sardinia and the Southern Netherlands at Utrecht/Rastatt/Baden (Brussels still under the Anglo-Dutch condominium until the 1716 handover); Hungary pacified at Szatmár 1711; Mantua annexed 1708.

realms.name: Duchy of Lorraine
realms.note: Restored to its duke at Ryswick 1697.

realms.name: Old Swiss Confederacy
realms.note: No single capital; the Diet met at Baden, then Frauenfeld after the Toggenburg War of 1712.

realms.name: Brandenburg-Prussia (Kingdom in Prussia)
realms.note: Royal title in Prussia since 1701; gained Upper Guelders at Utrecht; occupies Stettin by sequestration since 1713.

realms.name: Electorate of Saxony
realms.ruler: Frederick Augustus I (Augustus II the Strong)
realms.note: In personal union with Poland-Lithuania.

realms.name: Electorate of Bavaria
realms.note: Under imperial occupation 1704-1714; restored by Rastatt and Baden; the elector returned to Munich in April 1715.

realms.name: Electorate of Hanover (Brunswick-Lüneburg)
realms.note: In personal union with Great Britain since 1714; electoral dignity 1692.

realms.name: Electorate of Cologne
realms.note: Restored by the 1714 peace after exile.

realms.name: Duchy of Holstein-Gottorp
realms.ruler: Charles Frederick (a minor; regent Christian August of Eutin)
realms.note: Swedish ally; its Schleswig lands occupied by Denmark since 1713.

realms.name: Holy Roman Empire
realms.note: Listed for the emperor's title, as in 1600; the realms in it hold the land.

realms.name: Kingdom of Bohemia
realms.note: Habsburg crown land governed through the Bohemian Court Chancellery in Vienna.

realms.name: Kingdom of Hungary
realms.note: Reconquered from the Ottomans 1683-1699; Rákóczi's war ended at Szatmár 1711.

realms.name: Duchy of Milan
realms.note: Austrian since 1706; confirmed at Rastatt.

realms.name: Kingdom of Naples
realms.ruler: Charles VI (Viceroy Wirich Philipp von Daun)
realms.note: Austrian since 1707; confirmed at Rastatt.

realms.name: Kingdom of Sicily
realms.note: Ceded to Savoy at Utrecht; exchanged for Sardinia in 1720.

realms.name: Southern Netherlands (Anglo-Dutch condominium)
realms.ruler: Anglo-Dutch condominium council; sovereignty assigned to Charles VI
realms.note: Id kept from 1600. Assigned to Charles VI by Utrecht and Rastatt; the Barrier Treaty (Nov 1715) and the handover (Feb 1716) make it the Austrian Netherlands.

realms.name: Sultanate of Tidore
realms.note: VOC ally and vassal since 1667.

realms.name: Koch Bihar
realms.note: Lost its southern lands to the Mughals; Bhutanese influence at court. Ruler low confidence.

realms.name: Mutapa
realms.note: Much reduced, near the Portuguese Zambezi posts; capital point approximate.

realms.name: Savoy-Sicily
realms.ruler: Victor Amadeus II (King of Sicily since 1713)
realms.note: Gained Sicily and part of Montferrat at Utrecht; crowned in Palermo December 1713.

realms.name: Republic of Venice
realms.note: Holds the Morea since Karlowitz 1699; the Ottomans declared war on 9 Dec 1714.

realms.name: Republic of Genoa
realms.note: Holds Corsica.

realms.name: Order of St John (Malta)
realms.ruler: Grand Master Ramon Perellos y Roccaful
realms.note: On Malta since 1530; map id of the Knights of Rhodes.

realms.name: Denmark-Norway
realms.note: Re-entered the Great Northern War in 1709; holds Norway, Iceland, Schleswig; occupying Swedish Bremen-Verden.

realms.name: Swedish Empire
realms.note: Losing the Great Northern War: Livonia, Estonia and Finland occupied by Russia; Stralsund and Wismar about to be besieged.

realms.name: Tsardom of Russia
realms.note: Capital moved to Saint Petersburg in 1712; holds Livonia, Estonia and Finland by conquest; empire proclaimed only in 1721.

realms.name: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth (Crown of Poland)
realms.note: Restored in 1709 after Poltava; Saxon troops and Russian influence; Tarnogród Confederation forms late 1715.

realms.name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania
realms.note: Constituent of the Commonwealth with its own offices, treasury and army.

realms.name: Duchy of Courland and Semigallia
realms.ruler: Ferdinand Kettler (titular duke, absent); Dowager Duchess Anna Ivanovna in residence
realms.note: Polish fief under growing Russian control.

realms.name: Cossack Hetmanate
realms.note: Left-bank Ukraine under the Tsar since Pereiaslav 1654; Mazepa's revolt crushed 1708-1709.

realms.name: Kalmyk Khanate

capital.name: Ayuka Khan's camps on the lower Volga

realms.note: Nomadic; no fixed capital (the point is a rough centre of its pastures). Russian ally under treaty.

realms.name: Ottoman Empire
realms.ruler: Ahmed III (Grand Vizier Silahdar Damat Ali Pasha)
realms.note: Regained Azov at the Pruth 1711; declared war on Venice 9 Dec 1714 to retake the Morea.

realms.name: Principality of Wallachia
realms.note: Constantin Brâncoveanu executed in Constantinople Aug 1714; Phanariot rule begins 1716.

realms.name: Principality of Moldavia
realms.note: First Phanariot prince, installed after Dimitrie Cantemir fled with Peter I in 1711.

realms.name: Republic of Ragusa
realms.note: Tributary to the Sultan.

realms.name: Prince-Bishopric of Montenegro
realms.note: De facto self-governing highlands; Ottoman punitive campaign 1714.

realms.name: Regency of Algiers
realms.note: Ottoman suzerainty nominal; the dey also holds the title of pasha from 1711.

realms.name: Beylik of Tunis
realms.note: Husainid dynasty founded 1705.

realms.name: Regency of Tripoli
realms.note: Karamanli dynasty autonomous since 1711.

realms.name: Kingdom of Kartli
realms.ruler: Jesse (Ali Quli Khan); Vakhtang VI detained in Persia

realms.name: Kingdom of Imereti
realms.note: Ruler uncertain; the throne changed hands often in these years.

realms.name: Safavid Persia
realms.note: Weakened: Kandahar lost to the Hotaki Ghilzai in 1709; Baluch and Lezgin raids.

realms.name: Hotaki Kandahar
realms.note: Ghilzai revolt against the Safavids, April 1709; Mir Wais dies later in 1715.

realms.name: Khanate of Bukhara
realms.note: Weak khan; Uzbek amirs (Manghit, Kenagas) hold real power in the provinces.

realms.name: Khanate of Khiva
realms.note: Ruler uncertain for exactly this date (Shir Ghazi Khan reigned c.1714/15-1728).

realms.name: Kazakh Khanate
realms.note: Loosening into three juz; Dzungar pressure; Tauke's death date (1715-1718) is uncertain.

realms.name: Dzungar Khanate (Oirat)
realms.note: Choros-led Oirat state (map id oirat, as in 1600); rules the Tarim basin oases through khoja vassals since 1680.

realms.name: Khoshut Khanate (Tibet)
realms.note: Khoshut rulers of Tibet since Güshi Khan (1642); Lha-bzang deposed the Sixth Dalai Lama in 1706; the Dzungars kill him in 1717.

realms.name: Khalkha Mongols
realms.ruler: Tüsheet Khan and the Jebtsundamba Khutugtu (Qing banners)
realms.note: Submitted to the Kangxi Emperor at Dolon Nor 1691.

realms.name: Kingdom of Ladakh
realms.note: Tributary to the Mughals after 1684.

realms.name: Mughal Empire
realms.note: Late Mughal: after Aurangzeb's death in 1707 the provinces drift toward autonomy (Bengal under Murshid Quli Khan, the Deccan under Nizam-ul-Mulk); Banda Singh Bahadur's Sikh revolt in Punjab.

realms.name: Maratha Kingdom (Satara)
realms.note: Shivaji crowned 1674; split between Satara and Kolhapur after Shahu's release in 1707.

realms.name: Maratha Kingdom of Kolhapur
realms.note: Rival Maratha court; Tarabai imprisoned 1714.

realms.name: Kingdom of Kandy
realms.note: The Dutch VOC holds the coasts.

realms.name: Bhutan (Drukpa state)
realms.note: Unified by Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal from 1616.

realms.name: Kingdom of Kathmandu (Kantipur)
realms.note: One of three Malla kingdoms of the valley (with Patan and Bhaktapur); ruler for this date uncertain.

realms.name: Kingdom of Arakan (Mrauk U)
realms.note: Lost Chittagong to the Mughals 1666; court in disorder.

realms.name: Qing Empire
realms.note: Manchu dynasty; took Beijing 1644, ended the Three Feudatories 1681 and Zheng Taiwan 1683; Nerchinsk 1689.

realms.name: Joseon
realms.note: Tributary to the Qing since 1637.

realms.name: Tokugawa Japan
realms.ruler: Shogun Tokugawa Ietsugu (aged five; Arai Hakuseki and Manabe Akifusa govern); Emperor Nakamikado in Kyoto
realms.note: Tokugawa shogunate since 1603; maritime restrictions since the 1630s.

realms.name: Kingdom of Ryukyu
realms.note: Vassal of the Shimazu of Satsuma since 1609, and tributary to the Qing at the same time.

realms.name: Đại Việt (Lê dynasty, Trịnh lords)
realms.ruler: Emperor Lê Dụ Tông; Lord Trịnh Cương holds power

realms.name: Đàng Trong (Nguyễn lords)
realms.note: Nominally loyal to the Lê, in practice independent of the Trịnh; expanding into the Mekong delta.

realms.name: Thuận Thành (Champa remnant)
realms.note: Panduranga, autonomous under the Nguyễn since 1697.

realms.name: Kingdom of Cambodia
realms.ruler: Keo Fa III (Ang Em), with Nguyễn backing
realms.note: Contested: Thommo Reachea III fled to Ayutthaya in 1714 and returned with Siamese help later; ruler low confidence.

realms.name: Kingdom of Vientiane
realms.note: From the split of Lan Xang, 1707.

realms.name: Kingdom of Luang Prabang
realms.note: From the split of Lan Xang, 1707.

realms.name: Kingdom of Champasak
realms.note: Broke from Vientiane in 1713.

realms.name: Burma (Restored Toungoo dynasty)
realms.note: Map id of Ava used for the Restored Toungoo kingdom, whose capital has been Ava since 1635; Sane Min died in 1714.

realms.name: Sultanate of Johor
realms.ruler: Abdul Jalil Riayat Shah IV (Bendahara dynasty)
realms.note: Includes the Riau islands and Singapore island; capital location in 1715 uncertain.

realms.name: Sultanate of Mataram
realms.note: Installed with VOC help in 1705 and ceded territory to it; Surapati's sons still hold out in the Eastern Salient.

realms.name: Sultanate of Banten
realms.note: VOC protectorate since 1684.

realms.name: Sultanate of Gowa (Makassar)
realms.note: Bound to the VOC by the Treaty of Bongaya 1667.

realms.name: Sultanate of Ternate
realms.ruler: Sultan of Ternate (Amir Iskandar Zulkarnain Saifuddin; uncertain)
realms.note: VOC vassal; spice trade a Dutch monopoly.

realms.name: Zaydi Imamate of Yemen
realms.note: Holds Aden and the Tihama coffee ports (Mocha); Aden breaks away under Lahej later (c.1728).

realms.name: Ya'rubid Imamate of Oman
realms.note: Expelled the Portuguese from Muscat 1650 and Mombasa 1698; holds Swahili coast posts (Mombasa, Zanzibar, Pate).

realms.name: Ethiopian Empire
realms.note: Gondarine period; Yostos is a usurper (1711-1716).

realms.name: Kilwa Sultanate
realms.note: Omani suzerainty after 1698; status low confidence.

realms.name: Mogadishu
realms.note: After the Ajuran collapse; low confidence.

realms.name: Rozvi Empire (Changamire)
realms.note: Expelled the Portuguese from the plateau in the 1690s.

realms.name: Alaouite Morocco
realms.note: Alaouites since 1666; blockading Spanish Ceuta since 1694.

realms.name: Pashalik of Timbuktu (Arma)
realms.note: Descendants of the Moroccan conquerors of Songhai; independent of Morocco in practice since c.1660.

realms.name: Bamana Empire of Ségou
realms.note: Founded c.1712.

realms.name: Bornu Sultanate
realms.note: Ruler name low confidence.

realms.name: Kingdom of Dahomey
realms.note: Agaja succeeds in 1718.

realms.name: Asante Empire
realms.ruler: Osei Kofi Tutu I (death date disputed, 1712-1717)
realms.note: Founded c.1701 after victory over Denkyira.

realms.name: Kingdom of Kongo
realms.note: Reunited by Pedro IV in 1709 after the civil wars.

realms.name: Kingdom of Matamba (Ndongo-Matamba)
realms.note: Capital position approximate.

realms.name: Haudenosaunee (Five Nations)
realms.note: Neutral since the Great Peace of Montreal 1701; the Tuscarora move north to join them.

realms.name: Mapuche (Araucanía)
realms.note: Independent south of the Biobío frontier; point approximate.

realms.name: Imamate of Aussa
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised. Ends 1734.

realms.name: Mossi kingdoms
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

dublin.note: Kingdom of Ireland under the British crown.

bruges.note: Assigned to Charles VI by Utrecht and Rastatt, but governed by the Anglo-Dutch condominium until the handover of February 1716.

brussels.note: Assigned to Charles VI by Utrecht and Rastatt, but governed by the Anglo-Dutch condominium until the handover of February 1716.

barcelona.note: Taken by Philip V's army on 11 Sep 1714; Catalan institutions abolished by Nueva Planta (1716).

ceuta.note: Spanish since the Iberian Union (confirmed 1668); under Moroccan siege 1694-1727.

tunis.note: Husainid bey under nominal Ottoman suzerainty.

milan.note: Habsburg since 1706; confirmed at Utrecht and Rastatt.

palermo.note: Kingdom of Sicily given to Victor Amadeus II at Utrecht (1713); exchanged for Sardinia in 1720.

prague.note: Kingdom of Bohemia, a Habsburg crown land.

munich.note: Restored to the elector by Rastatt and Baden (1714); Imperial administration was ending and the elector returned in April 1715.

cologne.note: The city itself was a Free Imperial City, outside the Elector of Cologne's rule (his residence was Bonn).

bern.note: Canton of Bern within the Swiss Confederacy.

oslo.note: Christiania, in the Kingdom of Norway, ruled from Copenhagen.

konigsberg.note: Coronation city of the Kingdom in Prussia.

riga.note: Taken by Russia in July 1710; ceded at Nystad 1721.

vilnius.note: Grand Duchy of Lithuania within the Commonwealth.

kyiv.note: Kiev Governorate since 1708; the Hetmanate capital is Hlukhiv.

sarai.note: Lower Akhtuba steppe used by Kalmyk pastoralists under Russian suzerainty; Russian forts lie along the Volga.

caffa.note: Kefe, a directly ruled Ottoman province, not the Crimean khan's.

buda.note: Kingdom of Hungary under the Habsburgs since the reconquest of 1686.

belgrade.note: Ottoman again since 1690; taken by Eugene of Savoy in 1717.

athens.note: Venice held it briefly in 1687-1688 only.

tbilisi.note: Kingdom of Kartli, a Safavid vassal.

baghdad.note: Governor Hasan Pasha (1704-1724), founder of the Mamluk line.

cairo.note: Ottoman Egypt, with power held by the beys.

aden.note: Held by the Zaydi imams from 1645 until the Abdali of Lahej broke away c.1728-1731.

hormuz.note: Persian since the Anglo-Persian capture of 1622.

herat.note: Safavid until the Abdali Afghan revolt of 1716-1717.

samarkand.note: Nominally part of the Khanate of Bukhara; Uzbek amirs were largely autonomous.

urgench.note: Old Urgench (Kunya-Urgench) region in the Khanate of Khiva.

kashgar.note: Governed through Afaqi or Ishaqi khoja vassals of the Dzungars since 1680.

lahore.note: Lahore subah; Banda Singh Bahadur's Sikh revolt nearby.

gaur.note: Bengal subah under Murshid Quli Khan, who was already governing nearly independently (nawab from 1717).

mandu.note: Malwa subah under growing Maratha raids.

gulbarga.note: Bijapur subah of the Mughal Deccan (Nizam-ul-Mulk viceroy 1713-1715); Maratha chauth claims.

vijayanagara.note: Ruins of Hampi in the Mughal Bijapur-Carnatic; local power with poligars and the Afghan nawabs of Savanur.

lhasa.note: Lha-bzang Khan, recognised by the Kangxi Emperor.

karakorum.note: Orkhon valley of the Khalkha Mongols, Qing subjects since 1691.

kyoto.note: Seat of the emperor; governed by the shogunate's Kyoto shoshidai.

vijaya.note: Quy Nhơn area, in the Nguyễn south.

angkor.note: Siem Reap region of Cambodia; its throne was contested between Siamese- and Nguyễn-backed claimants.

pegu.note: Lower Burma under the Restored Toungoo court at Ava.

trowulan.note: East Javanese interior near Mojokerto; Surapati's descendants and the VOC also contested the east.

gao.note: Arma kaid at Gao, under Tuareg pressure.

niani.note: No state: Mande chiefdoms after Mali's collapse (Niani sacked c.1670); a Keita remnant ruled at Kangaba.

kanem.note: Kanem was governed for Bornu by the alifa of Mao; Bulala and later Wadai contested it.

great_zimbabwe.note: Southern plateau under the Changamire Rozvi.

kilwa.note: Kilwa sultan under loose Omani suzerainty after 1698.

mogadishu.note: Abgaal (Hawiye) imams after the Ajuran collapse.

zeila.note: Zeila's amirs depended on the Zaydi governors of Mocha; nominally Ottoman.

tenochtitlan.note: Mexico City, Viceroyalty of New Spain (colony).

santo_domingo.note: Spanish colony; the western third of Hispaniola is French Saint-Domingue.

bogota.note: New Granada (colony); the viceroyalty was created in 1717.

new_orleans.note: French Louisiana claim (capital at Mobile); New Orleans founded only in 1718; local peoples (Chitimacha, Houma, Acolapissa) on the ground.

sydney.note: No state: Eora nation; no European presence until 1788.

singapore.note: Sultanate of Johor; the island was sparsely settled by Orang Laut.

open_questions: Realm ids: Spain uses the map id 'castile' and Russia 'muscovy' as continuing states, and Great Britain keeps 'england' (id harmonisation: the 1707 Union is treated as England's continuation, as the README rule asks).

Southern Netherlands (Bruges, Brussels): held by 'burgundy' (the Burgundian and Habsburg Netherlands keep one id) as an Anglo-Dutch condominium under assigned Austrian sovereignty; a run may score it as Austria.
Munich: Bavaria was restored by the 1714 treaties, but the elector re-entered Munich only in April 1715; the exact handover date of the Imperial administration is unclear.
Cologne: the point is the Free Imperial City, not the Electorate (residence at Bonn); earlier checkpoints may have used the electorate.
Habsburg crowns follow the 1600 model: Bohemia, Hungary, Milan, Naples (overlord austria) and Sicily (overlord savoy) are separate realms holding their key places.
Vilnius is given to the Grand Duchy of Lithuania (overlord Poland); it could be scored as Poland.
Sarai (lower Akhtuba): Kalmyk pasture or Russian Astrakhan province; uncertain.
Kashgar: direct Dzungar rule or khoja vassal rule; the Afaqi-Ishaqi struggle is poorly dated.
Hampi (Vijayanagara point): Mughal Carnatic, Savanur nawabs or local poligars.
Trowulan: Mataram or Surapati's heirs in the Eastern Salient.
Angkor and the Cambodian throne: who reigned at Oudong on this exact date (Keo Fa III or Thommo Reachea III).
Kilwa, Mogadishu and Zeila: degree of Omani, Abgaal and Yemeni control is unclear.
Kanem (Njimi): Bornu governorship versus Bulala or early Wadai control.
New Orleans: not yet founded; given to French Louisiana by claim.
Uncertain rulers: Kathmandu (Mahindra Simha), Khiva (Shir Ghazi Khan), Ternate, Imereti, Bornu, Kazakh (Tauke Khan's death 1715-1718), Asante (Osei Tutu's death 1712-1717), Sharif of Mecca.

Formed list: the Qing keep the id 'jurchens' as the continuation of Nurhaci's Jianzhou state, and 'ming' ends; 'nguyen_lords' dates from 1600 itself (Nguyễn Hoàng's return south); 'arma_pashalik' was a Moroccan province in 1600 and independent only from c.1660. 'oirat' continues as the Dzungar Khanate.

Ended list judgement calls: 'mali' (Kangaba remnant survives), 'songhai' (Dendi remnant fades), 'transylvania' (Habsburg from the 1690s), 'lan_na' (Burmese province with vassal rulers until 1727), 'tokugawa' (became the government of 'japan'), 'adal' (Aussa imamate faded in the later 17th century).

Id harmonisation: Great Britain uses england; the Qing use jurchens (the map id of Nurhaci's Jianzhou Jurchen state, continued as Later Jin and Qing); Luang Prabang uses lan_xang (the royal line that becomes the Kingdom of Laos), with Vientiane and Champasak formed at the 1707–1713 split.
Added as still standing: the Imamate of Aussa (adal) and the Mossi kingdoms.
